findings.location: "label.required-label", the two required-field labels, lines 27 and 30
findings.evidence: <label class="required-label" for="address">Service address</label>, styled by .required-label { color: #cc0000; }; no asterisk, no required text, and no aria-required attribute appears on either field
findings.violation: Which fields are required is carried by label color alone, so a reader who cannot distinguish the red labels from the black ones has no way to tell the two required fields from the two optional ones before submitting.
findings.fix: Add a non-color signal to each required field: mark the label text itself (an asterisk with a legend, or the word required), and set required or aria-required on the input.

findings.location: "main > p:nth-of-type(2)", the instructional paragraph above the form, line 24
findings.evidence: Fields shown in red are required. Everything else is optional.
findings.violation: The instruction identifies the required fields only by their color, naming no label, no field, and no other identifier a reader who cannot perceive the color could use instead.
findings.fix: Name the required fields in the instruction, or point at the same non-color marker added for WCAG-1.4.1, for example fields marked with an asterisk are required.

findings.evidence:
Details

, introducing a section containing the service address, callback number, free-text notes, and account number fields
findings.violation: The heading does not distinguish this section from any other, so a reader scanning headings alone cannot tell that it is where the leak location and callback details are entered.
findings.fix: Rename the heading to describe what the section collects, for example Leak location and contact details.

findings.location: "span.error-text", the error message following the account-number field, line 38
findings.violation: The account-number field is marked aria-invalid="true" but its associated error text is a single generic word that names neither the field nor what is wrong with the value entered.
findings.fix: Replace the error text with one that names the field and the rule it failed, for example account number must be the 8 digits printed above your billing address.

note: The other four goldens all document scripted-lane output, so this one exists to show what the judged lane looks like on the same contract: golden-05.html is deliberately clean against all 13 scripted checks (running scripts/checks.py against it returns zero findings and a passing gate) while planting four defects only a reader can find. The form signals required fields with red label color and nothing else, which is WCAG-1.4.1's severity-3 anchor case because a color-blind reader cannot separate required from optional until submission; the instruction above the form then compounds it by pointing at that same color as its only identifier, which is WCAG-1.3.3 at severity 2 since every field still carries a readable text label. The Details heading fails WCAG-2.4.6 at severity 2, and it is reported at medium confidence rather than high because a generic heading is a judgment about what the section actually contains, which is exactly the calibration references/severity-anchors.md asks the judged lane to make. The account field is marked invalid with an error reading only the word Error, which WCAG-3.3.1 puts at severity 2 for a single field. Findings are ranked by severity, not by criterion ID, per the four-pass protocol's rank-and-bound step, and the single severity-3 finding fails the gate against the default zero threshold.
